# Introducing Specs: Markdown as a medium

Luke ZhangProduct Manager, Figma

Johnny DallasSoftware Engineer, Figma

Aosheng RanProduct Designer, Figma

 Inside Figma
 Product updates

We’re launching Specs, a container for your context that lives on the Figma canvas.

## Share Introducing Specs: Markdown as a medium

Turn existing Markdown into a spec by dragging and dropping any .md file onto the canvas. [...] Today, more and more product builders are working in Markdown, as collaborating with agents becomes more standard. It’s the de facto format for sharing context. But for all the context Markdown helps us express, it’s missing a lot of context, too. Markdown files tend to be single player on local computers, with brittle relationships to each other, and little tying them to the projects that spawned them. While most context is ephemeral, some context evolves into key inputs that need refinement over time and collaboration. That’s why we built Specs: a multiplayer container that allows context to fully express itself and move into, out of, and across Figma. [...] Connectors help bring outside context into Specs too. If you’re drafting a technical spec, for example, you can pull in context directly from your codebase with the GitHub connector. Or, say your team uses Hex for product usage data, and your PRD has an open question that data could answer. Select the question, add the Hex connector, and ask the agent to run the analysis and leave its findings as a comment on the spec. The answer lands in the document, right where the question was asked.

You can also drag in content from the Figma canvas, like a design exploration you riffed on with your team, or a diagram of a proposed user flow. Then, when you drag it back out, you can still preserve Figma properties.

## Ship data-backed websites with Payload

Payload is an open-source content framework for building internal tools, apps, and websites. In the past 12 months, Payload downloads have grown 6x, making it the fastest growing open source CMS on NPM.

Last year, the team behind Payload, an open source content framework, joined Figma [...] ## Shared context with Figma Specs

As teams increasingly collaborate with agents, Markdown is more ubiquitous than ever. But Markdown files have no relationship to each other, or to the projects they’re attached to. They also often have references to images, URLs, or even other Markdown files, which can be opaque to collaborators. That’s why we built Specs: a new native home for context, that allows it to fully express itself and move into, out of, and across Figma. [...] Specs can do a lot, from seeding generation of new directions, to creating data reports, to creating high fidelity PRDs, to handing off context to agents. You can bring in outside context with an agent, work together to turn rough ideas into a detailed spec, then send it to your coding agent using Figma’s MCP server, or use Specs to build a code layer and refine as you learn. Since Specs contain your shared decisions and reference your work on the canvas, you can codify and share context from diagrams, code layers, designs, and more.

Specs is starting to roll out today in open beta on web, desktop, and mobile and will be available on all paid plans.

results.title: Figma Specs: How to Give AI Coding Agents Better Context
results.content:
Figma describes Specs as a multiplayer container for Markdown that lives on the canvas. It is rolling out in open beta to paid plans on web, desktop, and mobile, and access is expanding gradually. Specs can embed FigJam files, frames, and code layers. Users can drag in existing .md files, duplicate a Spec for parallel work, and pull data through connectors such as GitHub. When a Spec is final, the team can hand it to a coding agent through the MCP server.

A screenshot shows how an interface looks. A Spec explains why it looks that way, how it behaves, and which frames and tokens govern each decision. For a simple button, the difference may be small. For a checkout flow or a permissions-based dashboard, it determines whether the agent builds the right thing. [...] Start with one interface. Write a focused Spec, connect a compatible agent, implement in small steps, and validate the result against the original design. Then update the Spec with what you learned.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Figma Specs?

Figma Specs is a Markdown container on the Figma canvas for requirements, design rules, and technical context. It can embed frames, FigJam files, and code layers, so written instructions stay linked to the design. It is in open beta for paid plans.

### How does Figma Specs work with AI coding agents?

A compatible coding agent connects to Figma through the MCP server and reads a Spec along with the frames it links to. The Spec supplies intent and rules, and the agent uses them to plan and write code. Human review is still required. [...] ## Quick Summary: What Figma Specs Changes for AI Coding

Figma Specs is a Markdown-based container on the Figma canvas. Teams use it to write requirements, design rules, and technical notes that people and connected AI agents can both read. The Figma MCP server lets compatible coding agents read a Spec along with the material it links to.

##### 2.    Write and refine specs together, on the canvas

Introducing Figma Specs, a container for context to move into, out of, and across Figma. Specs references work on the canvas—diagrams, code layers, designs, and more. It has all the features of a Markdown file plus collaborative, unique-to-Figma features, like the ability to embed a FigJam file, a frame, or any node from the canvas right in the spec, so text and designs sit side by side instead of living in screenshots or stale links. Now, teams and agents can bring written intent, visual explorations, and technical details together into a shared plan to guide agents from prototype to production. [...] Todayʼs announcements are designed to make it easier for entire product teams, including designers, developers and product managers, to work together in Figma. Code layers let teams explore and think through ideas by building them as code-backed prototypes on Figmaʼs multiplayer canvas. Figma Specs turn exploration into shared intent, so teams can align on what to ship and give agents clear direction to execute. And with Payload, teams can ship websites and internal tools backed by real data.

These announcements come one week after the launch of the Figma agent into general availability.

“The power of code layers, Figma Specs, Payload and everything weʼre launching today comes from what you can do with them together, with your team,ˮ said Field. [...] “Many look to Figma as the source of truth. With Figma Specs, bringing in a structured, formatted document thatʼs consistent across every file makes design files much more accessible and easier to follow for non-designers,ˮ said Mark Harvey, Staff Product Designer at Intuit.

# Figma Specs

Build with shared context across Figma, teams, and agents.

Get startedContact sales

## A container for context that can move into, out of, and across Figma.

Bring written intent, visual exploration, and technical details together for your team and your agents.

 Pull in your existing context, data, and codebase—no matter where it lives.

## Easily move between planning, designing, and coding.

Drop in data, connect external agents, and tag in teammates to help you build out your spec.

 

  ### Use Specs on the canvas or on its own

  Write out your spec where you design, or work in a separate space and drop it in when you’re ready. [...] ### Context that flows in both directions

  Pull in diagrams, tables, and designs from Figma. Or, bring in data and content from other tools via the Figma agent.

## Build with your favorite agent.

Specs gives agents structured Markdown to guide them from prototype to production.

 Tap the Figma agent to build with code layers on the canvas or ship to an external tool via MCP.
